question: secret
answer:
The benchmark keeps `NVIDIA_API_KEY` out of its result data by using it for the NVIDIA request’s `Authorization: Bearer` header and serializing only `ChatResult` fields, benchmark labels, metrics, and explicitly selected metadata. `Settings` and `Endpoint` also hide the key from their `repr`. [config.py](src/nvidia_ai/config.py#L26) · [llm.py](src/nvidia_ai/llm.py#L39) · [bench.py](src/nvidia_ai/bench.py#L205) · [bench.py](src/nvidia_ai/bench.py#L345)

If the server echoes the key, `redact()` replaces the exact credential and common API-key or bearer-token patterns with `***`. It scrubs errors before truncating them to 200 characters and scrubs generated content and reasoning when a stream succeeds. Tests cover an HTTP 401 that echoes the key and check that the test key is absent from every generated result file. [llm.py](src/nvidia_ai/llm.py#L21) · [llm.py](src/nvidia_ai/llm.py#L127) · [tests/test_llm.py](tests/test_llm.py#L88) · [tests/test_bench.py](tests/test_bench.py#L27)

There’s a gap in the “never” guarantee. A stream can fail after accumulating partial content or reasoning. The failure handler scrubs only the error message, and the benchmark still serializes those partial fields into `results.jsonl`. [llm.py](src/nvidia_ai/llm.py#L127) · [bench.py](src/nvidia_ai/bench.py#L205)
